published.title: Reuse spatial overlap counts across patch batches and channels
published.head: fcf7941c6efde888b612dbfdc8fc2b00790cfb93
published.body:
## What does this pull request do?

`combine_tensor_patches` currently unfolds and folds a full batch/channel-sized tensor of ones to count spatial overlap. Those counts depend only on image size, window, stride, and padding. This change constructs one `(1, 1, H, W)` count map and broadcasts the divisor across the reconstructed batch and channels.

The padding, folding, low-precision working dtype, complex handling, and final output conversion stay on their existing paths. A regression uses different overlapping patch values in two images and three channels, with independently calculated overlap averages and weighted input gradients.

## Related issue or discussion

This improves the existing fold-based reconstruction from #1603. It preserves the reconstruction/dtype behavior covered by #5960 and the empty-batch handling from #5674. Those changes did not share the overlap-count map. The current and former source paths, intermediate fork commits, and all-state upstream PR history were checked for an existing implementation.

## What did you check?

Local Pixi full pre-commit and type checks passed. The two affected patch test files pass all **207 tests** on the unchanged base and this candidate under both CPU Torch **2.5.1** and **2.15.0**.

[Independent CPU validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43940474557) compares exact base `cd2349f6` with candidate `2cf64717` on the same Ubuntu 24.04/Python 3.12 runner. It uses the shared benchmark helpers, warm-up, blocked-autorange medians, one CPU thread, and verifies the imported worktree. Output and input-gradient SHA-256 values match the base on all five benchmark workloads. The [validation script](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/947b2b5a71343c148e4673ea21b0e79e79881967/.validation/kornia-validate-cpu-candidates.py) and its benchmark inputs are retained outside the library diff.

| CPU workload (B×C×H×W; window/stride) | Torch 2.5.1 forward speedup | Torch 2.15.0 base → candidate | Torch 2.15.0 speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1×3×512×512; 32/16 | 1.54× | 36.48 → 26.77 ms | 1.36× |
| 8×3×256×256; 32/16 | 3.13× | 45.91 → 20.21 ms | 2.27× |
| 2×32×128×128; 16/8 | 1.30× | 35.41 → 24.27 ms | 1.46× |
| 4×64×128×128; 16/8 | 1.44× | 214.76 → 125.94 ms | 1.71× |

Forward-plus-backward speedups for those cases range from **1.12× to 2.12×** across the two versions. On Torch 2.15.0, summed positive profiler CPU allocations per forward fall by **37–56%**; the RGB batch goes from **109.9 to 50.8 MiB**. This is allocated-byte accounting, not peak process memory.

The single-image, single-channel control should not benefit: its count map already has the target shape. An initial shared-host forward/backward measurement was **0.85×**. Three interleaved base/candidate pairs on each independent runner were essentially flat: median ratios **0.997–1.001×**. These CPU measurements do not establish CUDA/MPS performance.

The selected CPU tests and measurements above are independent validation. The earlier local combined compile/ONNX invocation was blocked by automatic approval review after attempted runtime telemetry; that operation was not retried or moved.

After publication, Kornia's automatically triggered official checks on head `fcf7941c` completed the selected `augmentation` conformance suites: [compile: **45 passed**](https://github.com/kornia/kornia/actions/runs/43945723456/job/133575138116) and [ONNX: **83 passed**](https://github.com/kornia/kornia/actions/runs/43945723456/job/133575138105). These results were confirmed in the job logs. They do not establish CUDA/MPS performance.

The changelog fragment is `changelog.d/6802.fixed.md`.

## Which part was done by a human, if any?

Afloat16 set the contribution scope and required new, non-duplicate changes with practical benefit. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra Pro) performed the technical investigation, implementation, and validation reported above.

published.title: Accumulate mAP statistics before rounding low-precision outputs
published.head: f05f4d2c74d3d891c38d05ee1d33925a18bdca8b
published.body:
## What does this pull request do?

Keep detection counts, cumulative precision/recall, and the 11 VOC2007 precision samples in at least float32. The returned AP tensor and per-class values retain their existing output-dtype convention.

With bfloat16 boxes, **512 correct detections of 513 objects currently score AP = 1**, because the recall calculation rounds upward to the final threshold. The independent expected result is **10/11**, rounded only at output to **0.91015625**. The same discrete-threshold error occurs just below 0.5, and with float16 at 4096/4097. These examples use exactly representable coordinates in **[0, 124]**, spread across images with at most 128 boxes each; they do not rely on coordinate or IoU overflow.

The regression covers both threshold boundaries in float16/bfloat16 and float32/float64 controls. All detections are true positives, so attainable recall thresholds have precision 1: ten reached thresholds give 10/11, and five give 5/11. Matching and score ordering are unchanged. The docstring and breaking-change fragment describe the corrected low-precision scores.

## Related issue or discussion

#5101 corrected the construction of exact-tenth thresholds for float64; this fixes the separately rounded recall being compared with them. #5392 addressed geometric area overflow in IoU, and #5556 established input/output dtype promotion. Neither fixes these count/ratio decisions. Prior image-index caching work also leaves their dtype unchanged. The full upstream PR history and all reachable old fork versions were checked.

## What did you check?

Local Pixi full pre-commit and type checks passed. On exact base `cd2349f6`, the six new analytic regressions produce **4 failures and 2 passing controls**. On candidate `1f03856e`, the affected mAP and adjacent IoU files pass:

| Independent CPU environment | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Torch 2.5.1, Python 3.12, Ubuntu 24.04 | **327 passed, 1 skipped** |
| Torch 2.15.0, Python 3.12, Ubuntu 24.04 | **328 passed** |

The sole 2.5.1 skip is the unchanged `mean_iou` fullgraph bincount test requiring Torch ≥2.14. The selected files include eager, TorchScript, and native Dynamo `CompileCounter` capture tests. [Independent run and logs](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43940474557); [exact-base/candidate validation script](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/947b2b5a71343c148e4673ea21b0e79e79881967/.validation/kornia-validate-cpu-candidates.py). Each probe verifies its imported worktree.

This is a correctness change with a small measured cost, not a speedup claim. Four one-thread workloads (ordinary/near-full recall, float32/bfloat16) were **3.3–3.8% slower** in the Torch 2.5.1 run and within approximately **0.4%** in the Torch 2.15.0 run. The float32 controls showed comparable variation; these measurements do not isolate the cause. The near-full bfloat16 benchmark changes AP from **1 to 0.91015625** as required by the oracle. The source documents why wider statistics are necessary despite the retained low-precision output.

The selected CPU checks above are independent validation. The earlier local combined compile/ONNX invocation was blocked by automatic approval review after attempted runtime telemetry; that operation was not retried or moved.

After publication, Kornia's automatically triggered official checks on head `1673f23d` completed the selected `losses,metrics` conformance suites: [compile: **100 passed**](https://github.com/kornia/kornia/actions/runs/43945727480/job/133575113384) and [ONNX: **195 passed**](https://github.com/kornia/kornia/actions/runs/43945727480/job/133575113298). These results were confirmed in the job logs. No CUDA/MPS validation is claimed here.

The changelog fragment is `changelog.d/6803.breaking.md`.

## Which part was done by a human, if any?

Afloat16 set the contribution scope and required new, non-duplicate changes with practical benefit. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra Pro) performed the technical investigation, implementation, and validation reported above.
